More passes did not provide a general restoration improvement

Actual preferred v4 weights, unchanged. No training or clean reference enters prediction. Selection for general use remains single pass. The optional clean-only correction below is a separate validation-selected follow-up.

Rerunning an unchanged deterministic input produced identical outputs (maximum absolute difference: 0.0). Feeding the previous output back adds no new observations. A smoother or sharper-looking image does not establish recovered identity.

Three ways of using extra computation

  1. Literal cascading: 28→112→448→1792 pixels after 1,2,3 passes. For a fair comparison all outputs are resized to112 and measured against the same112 clean original.
  2. Fixed-size feedback: resize the previous result to28 and apply the model again, always returning112. Tested 2,3,5,8 passes.
  3. Self-ensemble: transform the same original input, predict separately, invert transformations and average. Tested 2,4,8 views; this is different from feeding predictions back.

Validation: first128 fixed images per condition

All methods use identical inputs and the same clean target. Three input conditions, 384 paired observations. PSNR/SSIM use float outputs; LPIPS/face-feature diagnostics use exported 8-bit pixels. Historical split reuse is disclosed. No restoration percentage or new full-QMUL recognition accuracy is claimed.

A limited alternative: clean-input consistency

One neural SR prediction is corrected three times using the discrepancy between the observed LR input and the downsampled reconstruction. The fixed correction step is0.2. No clean reference or identity label is used by the correction. This assumes clean bicubic downsampling and is not appropriate for unknown noisy camera degradation.

Clean-only focus was chosen after examining validation results and frozen before the following512-image test diagnostic. The all-profile selection remains single. The project has historically examined this test split; this is not a new untouched cohort. No per-image method selection or weight updates were made.

Mean LPIPS decreases by 3.51%. This is relative perceptual-distance reduction, not a percentage of image detail restored. The improvement is modest and is not a demonstrated human recognizability gain.

Better next steps

  • Use a larger native face crop with less compression and better exposure. Enlarging the same pixels does not add evidence.
  • For video, align and combine several actual frames: these can provide different observations. This requires source frames and a motion-aware video restoration method; it has not been implemented here.
  • For learned multi-step restoration, train a feedback/refinement network explicitly for repeated use. This feed-forward model was not trained as a recurrent refiner.
  • For the lightweight model, a separate teacher-distillation experiment could transfer useful detail from heavy models, with identity and eye/frame fidelity checks on held-out validation. That is a proposed training study, not a measured gain.

Sources: EDSR self-ensemble; trained SR feedback networks; input consistency/back-projection.
